Wow, this is going to feel harsh for $7, because MOST people do not live up to their ideals. I can say I am better than I was before. Since making a big life change a couple years ago (I retired), I am eating better, sleeping better, stress is reduced, I am exercising more and I am keeping up with medical appointments. So I am improving on the health and fitness axis, but I am still fat and out of shape and I haven't done the dental work I need. I began volunteering with an organization that raises guide dog puppies, so that hits supporting causes, community engagement, and to some extent, building relationships. But I am not working a paid job though I am still young enough that I could be, and I have some guilt about that. On the relationships axis, I am finally able to make time to work on friendships and family relationships. I've visited my elderly father twice since retiring and I'm touching base with friends more often. But again, could be doing more. On the legacy axis, I have gotten my finances cleaned up and I am making repairs and upgrades on my house, which had been deferred over the busier years. But I still need to work on an estate plan and I need to make a second go at cleaning out my junk so that the person who gets here at the end doesn't have a giant mess. 

I do spend far too much time on the internet and watching TV. I am disappointed in myself for that. But I'm a bit afraid to spend my nest egg, given how unsettled everything is. I know that time's a-wasting and there will come a time when I physically can't do these things. But's it's scary to start spending down that nest egg, give that we in the USA don't take care of our sick and elderly.

So yeah, I am still a work in progress.
